title: operational-readiness-for-multiwave-canaries-wip
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working note for an operational playbook to run multi-wave canaries and hybrid A/B experiments for the Console rollout and route-level model changes. The goal is to define a compact checklist, telemetry signals, automatic gating heuristics, and escalation path that SRE / Product / ML can use for low-risk progressive exposure.

Context and motivation:
- We increasingly need multi-wave canaries because model variants (quantized, distilled, prompt-tuned) behave differently across cohorts and latencies.
- Current 'single canary slice' approach sometimes misses regressions that show up under different client mixes (mobile vs web, region differences).
- This doc captures a proposal for operational readiness and the minimum telemetry and automation required to run 2–4 wave canaries safely.

Audience:
- Product owners launching model/response changes
- SRE and Oncall engineers who run rollouts
- ML engineers who own model variants and quality metrics
- Solutions/Support for customer-facing comms

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Canary wave definitions and slice selection guidance
- Core telemetry signals and alert thresholds (latency, error, quality, token economics)
- Automation knobs: traffic automation, time windows, quorum rules for progression/failback
- Post-mortem checklist and artifact collection requirements
- Known gaps and TODOs (experiments required)

Non-goals:
- Deep evaluation framework for semantic quality (covered by evals team)
- Cost optimization heuristics beyond simple unit thresholds

Definitions:
- Wave: discrete exposure stage (e.g., 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% traffic) with monitoring window and automated gating decisions.
- Cohort: user-slice by product surface (api-key, web vs mobile, region).
- Quorum: number of waves or cohorts required to pass before full rollout.

Proposed multi-wave plan (example):
- Wave 0 (smoke): internal-only traffic (canary orgs, product-test accounts). 1 hour window, high-sensitivity alerts.
- Wave 1 (narrow public): 0.2% randomized external traffic, include mobile-only slice. 4 hour window.
- Wave 2 (broad public): 2% randomized traffic, include region sampling and top-10 enterprise keys. 12 hour window.
- Wave 3 (ramped): 15% and then step to 50% if stable; automated ramping with guardrails.
- Final: 100% active.

Key telemetry signals (per-wave, per-cohort):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end) — track change vs baseline and absolute thresholds (p95 > baseline + 150ms => flag).
- Error rate: transport errors (5xx), model-timeout, decoding errors. Set both relative and absolute thresholds (e.g., >0.5% absolute or 3x baseline).
- Throughput/QPS and queue depth on the serving pool — sudden spikes indicate backpressure.
- Token cost per request — regression in tokens may indicate prompt engineering issue.
- Quality regressions: holdout prompt set pass rate and regression delta (absolute and population-weighted).
- Behavioral signals: high bounce/retry from clients, user-reported regressions (support tags).
- SLOs: % traffic meeting latency targets per-tier.

Suggested gating heuristics (automatable):
- Fail gate if any of the following occur within the monitoring window:
  - Absolute error rate > 0.75% for the wave cohort.
  - p95 latency increases 200ms+ vs baseline for 30m window.
  - Holdout eval pass rate drops by >3% absolute or 15% relative for critical prompts.
- Soft warnings (human review): token cost regressions >10%, bursty queue depth spikes without corresponding traffic increases.
- Quorum rule: at least 2 consecutive successful waves (no fail gates) including one that contains enterprise keys or geographic diversity before progressing to broad ramp.

Instrumentation and dashboards (minimum):
- Wave overview panel: current wave, % traffic, time since start, auto-decision countdown.
- Cohort overlays: per-cohort latency/error/throughput.
- Holdout eval results: small set of deterministic prompts (10–30) with pass/fail history.
- Alerting streams: high-priority (pager) for firm fail gates, lower-priority slack for soft warnings.

Automation mechanics (ops notes / runner integration):
- Rollout runner (github PR link above) should support staged manifests with: cohort selectors, initial percentage, step schedule, monitoring window, gating rules (as JSON predicates).
- When a fail gate triggers, runner must revert traffic within 2 minutes and create a rollback marker (incidents auto-created with runbook link).
- Allow 'manual hold' from Console (button) to pause automated progression.

Communication and escalation:
- Pre-launch channel: #rollout-signal with owners, SRE oncall, ML owner pinned.
- On fail gate: autopage SRE + ML primary; product owner gets slack mention and email.
- Post-rollback: incident doc auto-populated with artifacts: traces, sample requests, recent holdout fails, diff of model config.

Post-decision artifacts (required for finalizing rollout):
- Annotated runbook log (who clicked proceed, why), wave telemetry snapshot, holdout eval diff, linked support tickets (if any).
- Rollout review template (to be filled within 48 hours) with: root cause hypothesis, mitigations, next-steps for future rollouts.

Risk matrix (quick):
- Latency regressions -> impacts SLAs and user experience. Mitigate with prefix caching, reverting to previous model variant, throttling.
- Semantic regressions -> invisible to latency but high product risk. Mitigate with holdout evals and conservative quorums.
- Cost regressions -> may be acceptable short-term; set budget cap alarms to avoid runaway spend.

Checklist for runbook readiness (pre-launch):
- [ ] Wave manifest checked into rollout-runner repo with correct cohort selectors.
- [ ] Holdout eval set up and verified (smoke pass on internal infra).
- [ ] Dashboards created and shared with SRE and product.
- [ ] Pager rules and slack channels configured.
- [ ] Backout image or model variant pinned and tested.
- [ ] Communication plan prepared (customer comms + internal).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we weight holdout eval failures from less-common cohorts? (TODO: propose weighting scheme)
- Should enterprise keys be excluded from automated progression and require manual signoff? (tradeoff: slower but safer)
- Can we add lightweight A/B metrics (user satisfaction proxy) to the service to detect semantic drift early? Need engineering estimate.
- Need runbook template in Confluence to match data artifacts (linked_artifacts above is placeholder).

Small experiment proposals to validate assumptions:
- Run 50 small canaries (0.1% each) across different cohorts over 2 weeks to learn cohort-specific variance.
- A/B shadow test where new variant sees duplicated traffic but does not affect responses; measure latency and holdout eval pass rate.

Next steps (near-term):
1) Align on gating thresholds with SRE (owner: Luis Ortega) by 2025-10-07.
2) Implement Wave manifest schema for rollout-runner (owner: DevOps, PR target: #412).
3) Create the Dashboard template and pipe required metrics (owner: Mei Chen) by 2025-10-14.
4) Run small internal smoke canary with feature-flagged traffic and validate rollback timeline (owner: Asha).

Notes to self:
- Keep the first public wave conservative; we learned from last quarter that top-10 enterprise keys are brittle.
- Avoid over-tuning gating thresholds to the point where nothing can ever progress.

References and helpful links:
- Regression detection primer (internal): Confluence link (placeholder)
- Rollout-runner repo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-runner/pull/412
- Slack thread: #rollout-signal (search: "multiwave experiment")

End of working notes. This is intentionally rough — fill gaps and convert to shared runbook when stable.
